title: Universal conormal vanishes on an open isomorphism locus
statement: Let h:Z -> S be formally unramified [def-weil-pbc-formally-unramified-morphism] and let i:Z -> Z′, s:Z′ -> S be a universal first order thickening [def-weil-pbc-universal-first-order-thickening]. For an open immersion j:T -> Z [def-weil-open-immersion] such that j followed by h is an isomorphism, the tensor pullback j* C_h [def-pc-module-pullback, def-weil-pbc-conormal-sheaf-formally-unramified] is a zero object. All objects are schemes [def-pc-scheme].

source.place: Tag 04FA and Tag 04FF, calculation of the conormal on the open image of the diagonal

proof.text: Take V = j(T), U = S, and identify T with V by isoOpensRange. Universal thickening open restriction supplies a universal thickening of hV : V -> S and an isomorphism from the restricted C_h to its conormal. The equation identifying hV with j followed by h proves hV is an isomorphism.

For a universal thickening iV of an isomorphism hV, construct r = sV followed by the inverse of hV. The compatibility equation gives iV followed by r = id. Apply the universal lifting uniqueness to the thickening itself to show r followed by iV = id. Thus iV is an isomorphism and its kernel ideal is bottom. Its ideal module is zero: its sectionwise injective inclusion has image killed by the isomorphism to the closed subscheme. Tensor pullback preserves zero objects by its adjunction.

Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies tensor pullback along V.ι with restriction along V.ι. Pull the zero restricted conormal back along T ≅ V; the composition comparison and isoOpensRange_hom_ι identify the result with j* C_h.

lean.statement:
theorem open_iso_conormal_isZero {Z S Z' T : Scheme.{u}} (h : Z ⟶ S)
    [FormallyUnramified h] (i : Z ⟶ Z') (s : Z' ⟶ S)
    (H : IsUniversalFirstOrderThickening h i s)
    (j : T ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j] [IsIso (j ≫ h)] :
    IsZero ((Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback j).obj
      (formallyUnramifiedConormal h i s H))
